Industrial robots

Everoyal reports pilot production of robot enclosures

The Suzhou supplier describes roughly 60-unit revisions and combined casting, machining, printing and sheet-metal processes.

RoboticsTomorrow ↗23 October 2026English editorial summary
Story

Moving beyond display parts

Suzhou Everoyal Precision says its humanoid and service-robot enclosure work has moved into pilot production, typically around 60 units per revision. Its October 23 announcement describes a batch size, not sales or deliveries of complete robots.

Processes under one roof

The company reports a 10,000-square-meter facility with two lines and over 50 machines covering vacuum casting, CNC machining, 3D printing, sheet metal and rapid tooling. Covers, mounting faces and brackets can move between processes without changing suppliers.

Inspection and remaining unknowns

Everoyal says prototypes and machined parts receive 100% inspection using Zeiss CMM and ROMER equipment, with reports. Batch work uses 5% random inspection at an agreed depth. Customers, delivery schedules and independent results are undisclosed, so these remain supplier-reported capabilities.
